concept.name: Gross exposure
concept.definition: The total absolute value of a portfolio's long and short positions, conventionally expressed as a percentage of capital: long exposure plus short exposure, without netting. Values above 100% indicate the use of leverage.
concept.intuition: It measures how much exposure the fund is carrying in total — the gross weight on the scale, regardless of how the bets offset each other.
concept.mechanics: Sum the absolute market values of all long and short positions and divide by net asset value. Gross exposure is the usual base for management-fee calculation and the direct gauge of how much capital is at work and how levered the book is.
concept.formula: Gross exposure = (|long positions| + |short positions|) / net asset value * 100%.
concept.failure_modes: Gross exposure says nothing about direction or hedging quality: a 250% gross book may be tightly hedged or one basis trade from disaster. It also treats all positions alike, ignoring their individual volatilities and correlations.
concept.misconceptions: Low net exposure does not mean low risk if gross exposure is high — a 0% net, 300% gross fund can lose heavily when longs and shorts move adversely at once — and gross above 100% by definition means leverage is in use.
concept.example: A fund with $200M capital holding $350M long and $150M short has gross exposure of $500M, or 250% of capital.
